scope: Five focused comparison lanes, supplied Falling Sky rules and thirteen adopted provisional rulings, independent reproduction and held-out gameplay.

validation.balance_note: Fresh full suite includes the existing 15-game legacy balance canary (seeds 1–3, 40-point band). No fresh 100-game guardrail was run and the baseline is unchanged. All 14 prior GitHub checks passed on the audited commit.

findings.conclusion: Sappers target and admission errors confirmed by seven natural wrong-target and two empty-Event witnesses; supplied Roman/Aedui per-card priorities and explicit controls agree.
Drought wrong-region selection confirmed by twelve natural dispatch witnesses and exact-target controls across base and expansion instructions.

Seventeen-case finalized probe confirms omitted Slingers in three ordinary bot forecast gates; public casualty choices prove opening Leader Loss, with six absent-Capability, three surviving-force and two Stalwart controls.
Aedui three-destination plan collapses to one three-Warband move, while the explicit three-group control satisfies 8.6.5 at identical Resource cost.
Aedui March cost makes Trade required and profitable, but initial No SA suppresses post-Command evaluation; exact movement with opened live SA gate gains 12 Resources.

NP Cisalpina fallback chooses removal of three Legions despite an unrestricted legal Home destination. Complete §8.4 maximum-action and move-own guidelines support preserving the force, and the legal human allocation enables the explicitly required expedition.

Within the same Mandubii Region, NP Belgae/Romans remove the Alesia City Ally before Senones ordinary Ally. The reverse §8.4.1 priority and physical tribe mapping agree with the human exact-removal control.

independent_review.source_review: Supplied rules, actual code, canonical pieces, before/after census and structure, public entrypoints, exact matched controls and previous-audit scope reviewed.
limits: LC12-01 relies on the complete non-player movement and maximum-action guidelines plus scenario relocation. The parenthetical voluntary-removal reference alone is insufficient because §1.4.1 also covers reclamation.

Battle fixtures prove possible Leader Loss via public Slingers casualty requests. The diagnostic Command-aware prediction may include hypothetical Counterattack after all attackers are gone; that value is not treated as live loss arithmetic.
Frontend controls cover real terminal collection, typed response validation and serialized-state replay. They do not claim a durable pending SeatSession interaction.
Constructed positions establish particular defects, not their frequency in randomly sampled play.
independent_review.portable_note: Independent scripts are copied away from their author directories and take an explicit repository path. All copies and outputs match final author files; final archive extraction is checked separately by the lead.

findings.title: Unshaded Sappers ignores non-player target restrictions and admits Events without a Citadel target
findings.expected: Base Roman Sappers targets Arverni then Belgae and excludes Aedui. Base Aedui Sappers targets player Arverni or Belgae only. If no legal Citadel target can lose Resources, the Non-player must continue its Command flowchart.
findings.actual: Seven natural dispatch/execution cases drain the wrong Faction. Romans and Aedui drain Aedui instead of player Belgae in four cases. Aedui drain Non-player Arverni instead of player Belgae in three cases. Two no-Citadel Pax Gallica cases select and execute an Event with no game effect.
findings.root_cause: _EVENT_PARAM_DERIVERS has no numeric24 producer. The handler falls back to the first Citadel faction in GALLIC_FACTIONS, ordered Arverni, Aedui, Belgae. Generic REMOVES_RESOURCES effectiveness returns true without checking the Citadel or printed target conditions.
findings.comparison: Liberty or Death base_bot._is_ineffective_event executes a copied Event and checks semantic effects. Waxhaws ranks eligible targets under its printed priorities while preserving explicit targets. These patterns expose the distinction between a legal generic fallback and a legal Non-player choice. Falling Sky source text supplies the actual target rules.
findings.reproduction: Run probe_events.py --repo <audited checkout>. EV12-01 includes four Aedui-versus-Belgae cases (Pax Romans and Aedui in all three base scenarios), three NP-Arverni-versus-player-Belgae cases, and two empty-target cases. All actions originate in dispatch_bot_turn and resolve through execute_decision.
controls: Seven identical-board explicit Belgae target plans remove the correct Resources.
One Roman Arverni-over-Belgae priority control succeeds.
Two can_play_event=False controls execute normal non-Pass Commands.
Every public execution passes pre/post census and structural validation. should_decline_event preserves the complete encoded board and RNG.
findings.prior_overlap: Round5 report line63 explicitly held exploratory Sappers targeting leads outside its confirmed count. This audit supplies the missing public reproductions, source proof and controls. It extends the missing NP selector class of BE7-02 and EV11-02/03 to numeric24. Earlier human Sappers casualty/choice work concerns authored and shaded effects. No closed finding is reopened.
findings.limits: Scenario-derived legal synthetic positions. Citadels are placed at canonical Cities through _unally_tribe/_ally_tribe(citadel=True), using physical stock. No full gameplay history or natural encounter rate is claimed. Only base numeric24 unshaded targeting is counted. Expansion A24 and shaded Sappers are excluded. The no-target admission cases have zero Citadels, avoiding any ambiguity about faction priorities when Resources are zero.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a numeric24 Non-player target selector and matching pure availability check based on current Citadels, Resources and printed Roman/Aedui instructions. Keep human exact targets available and preserve shaded casualty handling. Treat target selection and admission as one card contract repair.

findings.title: Non-player Drought places its marker by map order and removes forbidden targets
findings.expected: Romans place Drought to remove player Arverni/Belgae in base or player Germans/Belgae in expansion, with no Roman loss. Aedui select only player Arverni/Belgae in base or player Germans/Belgae in expansion. A legal player-only Carnutes target exists in every witness.
findings.actual: All twelve natural Event executions place Devastated at Morini, removing a Non-player Belgic piece and leaving the eligible player piece at Carnutes. The six Roman cases also remove their own Auxilia at Morini, contrary to the explicit instruction. All twelve exact Carnutes controls remove the player opponent and preserve Morini.
findings.root_cause: Numeric49 has no NP parameter deriver. execute_card_49 defaults missing devastate_region to marker_regions(state)[0], which is Morini on these maps, ignoring the instruction text already carried by the bot action.
findings.comparison: Liberty or Death handlers build eligible targets and rank them before seeded tie selection. Its ineffective-event preview alone would not catch this Drought error because both a wrong and a correct target cause effects. The comparison directs review toward preserving target priorities as well as actual-effect checks.
findings.reproduction: Run probe_events.py --repo <audited checkout>. EV12-02 covers Romans/Aedui in Pax Gallica, Ariovistus and Gallic War at game seeds1/7. Each board has NP Belgae at Morini and an eligible player enemy at Carnutes. Roman cases add one Auxilia at Morini.
controls: Twelve identical-board explicit devastate_region=Carnutes controls remove exactly one legal player piece, preserving Roman and NP Belgic pieces at Morini.
All Resources halve correctly in natural and control executions.
All pre-existing markers match exactly with only the selected Devastated marker added.
All public executions pass census and structural integrity before and after. Natural Event admission leaves the encoded board/RNG unchanged.
Outputs match byte for byte at PYTHONHASHSEED=0 and987.
findings.prior_overlap: The earlier human-choice Drought finding repaired casualty ownership and requests. Those owner choices remain functional in these probes. This concerns the separate NP marker-location producer. Earlier German Drought movement work concerns Command priorities after devastation. EV11-03 is a similar missing printed selector on another card, whose repair remains complete.
findings.limits: Curated scenario-derived legal positions, with no existing Devastated markers. In Pax, one Available Arverni Warband is placed in Carnutes. In expansion, the original German Warband moves from Morini to Carnutes, and the original Arverni Warband there moves to Arverni. Roman cases place one Available Auxilia at Morini. Helpers preserve stock, tribe synchronization and Control. These probes do not prescribe the ambiguous fallback when no instructed player-only Region exists, and do not estimate ordinary-play frequency.
findings.suggested_fix: Derive the Drought marker Region using the executor-specific base/expansion opponent and player-seat filters, Roman casualty exclusion, then the existing general NP priority and seeded tie helpers. Preserve owner casualty selection and Resource halving. Add controls for legal remaining targets before addressing any absent-target policy.

findings.title: Belgae, Arverni and German Battle gates omit Balearic Slingers opening fire
findings.expected: Decline the threat Battle when four Roman Auxilia with unshaded Slingers would first assign two Losses to a named Leader and his sole Warband. Apply the printed no-Leader-Loss gate and continue to the faction’s March path.
findings.actual: At seeds 1 and 7 all three bots dispatch Battle. Belgae and Arverni add Ambush. Public execution removes the sole Warband and named Leader before their Attack, preserves all four Roman Auxilia, and charges one Resource. The logged casualty requests explicitly offer the Leader Loss.
findings.root_cause: The three ordinary bot gates call predict_battle without earlier_battles, so its conditional opening-fire stage is skipped. Existing Command-aware prediction identifies the possible Leader Loss. Live Slingers execution is correct.

Only Slingers is dynamically established; other Capability omissions remain static leads. German Command-aware diagnostic also includes hypothetical Counterattack after the attackers are gone; the public casualty requests prove the two opening Losses, which alone violate the Leader-safety rule.
findings.suggested_fix: Supply prospective Command context and prior selected Battles to all affected gates, include opening losses and actual remaining force in Leader safety, and preserve once-per-Command Roman choice and Stalwart cancellation. Add public dispatch regressions with controls.

findings.title: Non-player Interlude evacuation removes every Cisalpina force despite legal Home destinations
findings.expected: Apply the general Non-player move-own priorities and maximum execution guideline to the scenario relocation. Move Roman Legions from Cisalpina to their legal Home Region Provincia. With all six on-map Legions preserved, the otherwise-equipped NP Romans must conduct the Britannia expedition.
findings.actual: In three full third-Winter cases, NPC Rome removes three Cisalpina Legions to the Legions Track despite Provincia being a legal destination. Only three Legions remain on map, so the expedition fails, Belgae receive Britannia forces and the Senate moves to Uproar. Three human default-delegation cases repeat this. Three explicit legal relocation controls and three already-home controls conduct the expedition, put three Legions in the Harvest box and three in Britannia, and move the Senate to Adulation.
findings.root_cause: _cisalpina_relocation calls the human agent when appropriate but defaults every remaining allocation to destination=None. It bypasses the existing gallia_evacuation.default_response, which prioritizes relocating own pieces and uses removal only when legal destinations are exhausted.

The phase cursor is controlled.

Retain human removal options, forced removal when no Home slot exists, faction order, Roman Legion Track destination on actual removal, Gallia Togata bypass and the expedition check on surviving forces.

findings.title: Non-player Interlude Ally reductions remove a City Ally before a non-City Ally
findings.expected: After choosing a Region under the Interlude ordering, apply §8.4.1 reverse own-removal priority. When removing two of three own Allies at Mandubii, Lingones and Senones, retain the Mandubii City Ally and remove the two ordinary Allied Tribes.
findings.actual: Across three seeds each for NP Belgae and NP Romans, whole third-Winter execution removes Lingones then Mandubii and retains Senones. The six identical-board human allocation controls retain Mandubii. Two Carnutes/Aulerci controls happen to retain the City because the ordinary Tribe sorts first.
findings.root_cause: The general and Roman NP reduction loops remove an anonymous ALLY then call clear_allied_tribe without a Tribe selection. That bookkeeping helper iterates alphabetical Tribe names and only protects a City when a Citadel remains. It does not implement own-loss priorities, so the second mandatory removal clears Mandubii before Senones.

findings.title: Aedui spreading March collapses three one-Warband groups into one large move
findings.expected: Section 8.6.5 first sends one Hidden Aedui from one origin into each of up to three eligible adjacent Regions, while keeping one Warband and existing Aedui Control at the origin. On the witness board four Hidden Aedui at Mandubii can send one each to the three destinations already chosen by their own planner, retaining one. No Warbands remain movable for an additional Control step.
findings.actual: Public dispatch selects March and spread_destinations Atrebates, Treveri and Carnutes. Public execution sends all three movable Warbands only to Atrebates. Treveri and Carnutes remain empty. All four natural command-only cases (two scenarios, two seeds) do this. Four matched explicit three-group player controls place one in each destination for the same two-Resource origin charge and retain Mandubii Control.
findings.root_cause: node_a_march records destinations without concrete one-Warband groups. The shared plan_expand_march_moves combines Control and spread destinations, visits each origin once, chooses one nearest destination and sends every Warband beyond the leave-behind. Its nonempty-effect check only asks whether any group can move, so the malformed allocation passes.

sources.detail: Section 8.6.5 one Hidden Warband per spreading destination, then minimum Control movement, keeping last Warband and Control.
Section 3.3.2 permits multiple groups from one origin, charges once per origin, flips Revealed pieces before moving.

comparison_refs.detail: Patriot spread phase constructs one-Militia groups for each destination and tracks already committed source pieces.
Aggregates source removals for a Control check and sends explicit move_plan groups into the March executor.

findings.reproduction: PYTHONHASHSEED=0 python probe_bots.py --repo /absolute/fs-bot. Cases spread_collapsed and explicit_three_groups_control, Pax Gallica? and The Great Revolt, seeds 6 and 19.
findings.controls: Four explicit three-group controls use normal execute_decision player_action, charge exactly two Resources once at Devastated Mandubii, preserve one origin Warband and Control, and add Hidden Aedui plus Control at all three destinations. Every probe has clean pre/post census and structural checks. Dispatch preserves board and RNG on these fixtures. All 24 output records are identical across hash seeds 0 and 987.
findings.prior_overlap: Prior comparative ledgers through round11 inspected. NP11-02 concerns a German expansion advance and was repaired using explicit groups. Existing Aedui unit tests inspect node plans, including spread_destinations, without asserting the three resulting arrivals. NP8-02 addressed Aedui Rally ability timing. FE6-02 concerned human Enlist split German March. This newly proved ordinary Aedui allocation path is distinct.
findings.limits: Sparse canonical mid-year boards initialized through build_initial_state, not untouched setup_scenario boards or a reconstructed full game history. The single Devastated marker represents a prior Arverni action. The probe does not invoke Winter victory or estimate natural frequency/balance. No Event, terminal, saved-session, expansion Leader or human Supply-disagreement claims. No independent allegation about additional Control movement, Scouted spreading, Diviciacus ordering or other faction expander consumers is counted.
findings.suggested_fix: Build executable Aedui groups in printed phase order on a projected board. Reserve one eligible Hidden-arrival Warband per spread destination, retain source Control and leave-behinds, then compute the additional minimum Control move from remaining unmoved pieces. Preserve origin billing and separate expansion Leader rules. Add result-level regressions rather than asserting only planner destination lists.

findings.title: Aedui March drops the post-Command Trade opportunity when its initial Suborn choice is empty
findings.expected: Section 8.6.5 requires Trade or Suborn after March, following the current-state test in 8.6.3. Here March reduces Aedui Resources from 10 to 8, enabling the below-ten Trade condition. Non-player Roman agreement and the resulting Aedui Control yield twelve Resources under 4.4.1, producing 20 Resources after the demonstrated move.
findings.actual: With only Revealed Aedui present, public dispatch emits March with No SA and translates it as command-only. March executes and pays two Resources, then stops at eight Resources. The current ordinary Trade chooser returns Trade worth twelve. Changing only the preselected SA label to Suborn opens existing live rederivation, which itself chooses Trade and produces twenty Resources. Starting with Hidden Aedui also naturally reaches this correct live rederivation.
findings.root_cause: node_a_march calls only _determine_suborn_sa on the pre-March board. It carries no deferred Aedui post-Command intent when the returned label is No SA. The translator therefore chooses command-only. _execute_sa_confirmed returns on No SA, before the existing Aedui current-state Trade/Suborn branch can run.

sources.detail: Section 8.6.3 tests Resources at the moment the SA resolves and, if Trading, obtains all possible Resources.
Section 8.6.5 explicitly applies Trade or Suborn after March, excluding Britannia crossings.
Section 4.4.1 Supply Lines and Roman agreement yield two Resources for each qualifying item.

comparison_refs.detail: Patriot _march_chain executes March first and then invokes its ordinary special-activity chain against the completed state when authorized.
The post-Command chain checks actual current Resources before choosing activities.

findings.reproduction: PYTHONHASHSEED=0 python probe_bots.py --repo /absolute/fs-bot. Cases new_trade_omitted, live_trade_dispatch_control, existing_hidden_sa_control and command_only_control across Pax Gallica? and The Great Revolt at seeds 6 and 19.
findings.controls: Four source-required SA-label controls retain exact March moves and allow existing live rederivation to choose actual Trade, yielding twelve Resources. Four natural Hidden-force positive controls reach the same Trade without label changes. Four command-only controls correctly execute only the March at two Resources. Ordinary Trade forecasting and dispatch are board/RNG pure in these fixtures. All before/after census and structural checks pass.
findings.prior_overlap: Newly demonstrated ordinary Aedui March consumer of the post-Command opportunity defect class. NP8-02 repaired Aedui Rally, NP9-02 Arverni Rally/Belgic Raid, NP10-01 Arverni March and NP11-01 Belgic March. Those repair paths remain covered. This finding does not reopen their repaired consumers.
findings.limits: Sparse canonical mid-year boards initialized through build_initial_state, not untouched setup_scenario boards or a reconstructed full game history. The single Devastated marker represents a prior Arverni action. The probe does not invoke Winter victory or estimate natural frequency/balance. No Event, terminal, saved-session, expansion Leader or human Supply-disagreement claims. This proof uses the existing movement result to isolate the missing SA. NP12-01 may change that board and Trade yield when repaired, so a repair regression should compute the correct post-March yield. The public natural failure alone establishes the bug. The label control is an explicit diagnostic, not a claimed unmodified dispatch.
findings.suggested_fix: Carry an authorized deferred Aedui post-March ability decision or reliably forecast the completed board. Reuse the existing current-state Trade-to-Suborn choice and actual Supply declarations even if no pre-Command Suborn exists. Preserve true command-only restrictions and apply Britannia exclusion to actual executed crossings.
